passage:
The city began collecting food scraps from homes and turning them into compost for parks and farms.
Some families joined quickly. Others disliked the smell or did not know what could go into the bin.
The city gave out small kitchen containers, clear guides, and free compost bags for gardens. Participation improved.
Students visited the compost center and saw food waste becoming dark soil.
The process changed how they saw leftovers. Banana peels and vegetable ends were no longer just trash. They could return nutrients to the ground.
Composting is a quiet circle. What once came from soil can help soil again.
